confusions: Sub-location entrances for major quest sites (the Hundred Gallery in Cinderhall, the Drowned Nave in Fenmarch, the Kings' Rest in Hollowbrook) were not discoverable by exploring nearby rooms directly — only a specific NPC's 'bearings'/dialogue line gave exact directions ('north four, then east one'), and I wasted 30-60 turns wandering undifferentiated spoil/mound/reed rooms before finding the right NPC to ask.

The 'Which King' mystery (Hollowbrook) scattered its 3 evidence sources (ring-ditch, mere-stone, causeway stone) across distant, non-obviously-connected map nodes with no indicator of how many total clues existed until all were found.

Large hub regions (Cinderhall's downs, Fenmarch's fen, Hollowbrook's barrows) have many rooms with near-identical flavor text and no persistent map/bearings summary, making backtracking disorienting despite a working 'travel to known place' shortcut.
suggestions: Make a 'get bearings' or equivalent free action available in every hub area (not just select rooms) so players can always orient toward known quest destinations.
When a quest names a destination ('north of Cinderhall, past the fall'), consider surfacing exact turn-by-turn directions in the quest log itself rather than requiring a separate NPC dialogue query.
For multi-clue mysteries (like Which King), tell the player up front how many total pieces of evidence exist so they know when they can stop searching.

Escalating-DC retry checks (e.g. the skiff drag, which went DC14→15→16 across fails) can feel like a slow-motion softlock risk for low-stat builds; consider capping the escalation lower or offering an alternate free route sooner.
